thread:
Chris W: Heads up — CI size spike after landing the new attention kernels. Build artifact went from 42MB -> 97MB on linux-x86 with nvcc 12.2. Suspect some PTX/fatbin duplication across sm targets.
Dana L: Ugh. Any immediate build logs?
Chris W: Pasting the nvcc invocation we use in the matrix:
```
nvcc -arch=sm_70 -gencode=arch=compute_70,code=sm_70
     -gencode=arch=compute_80,code=sm_80
     -Xfatbin --compress-all -O3 -lineinfo -Xcompiler -fPIC
```
Chris W: We added `-gencode compute_80` to support new kernels, but I think we ended up embedding PTX+SASS for multiple archs.
Olivia M: Did we enable `-gencode=arch=compute_80,code=compute_80` anywhere? that would keep only PTX which is heavier on JIT but smaller on binaries.
Chris W: Not in this matrix. We're producing fatbins for sm_70/sm_80/sm_86 which duplicates a lot of object sections.
Sophie R: Could also be LTO / link-time codegen pulling in multiple instantiations. Are we doing `-flto` on that target?
Chris W: Not explicitly but our CMake uses `-O3` and the toolchain provider added `-flto` for release builds recently.
Tyler K: For context: the new attention kernels include templated instantiations for different tile sizes which expand binary quite a bit if multiple sm variants get compiled.
InfraBot: CI job #4221: build/linux-x86/shrink-check FAILED — artifact size 97MB > threshold 60MB
Dana L: Quick triage options: 1) restrict gencode list in CI (whitelist sm targets we actually run on), 2) build PTX-only for some variants, 3) split artifacts per-sm, 4) disable LTO on CI.
Olivia M: I'd prefer whitelist + PTX for older variants. That keeps runtime fallback while reducing duplication. e.g., `-gencode=arch=compute_86,code=sm_86 -gencode=arch=compute_80,code=compute_80`
Sophie R: Splitting artifacts is also attractive for caching but complicates packaging and runtime kernel lookup.
Chris W: Agreed. Runtime supports multiple fatbin search paths but packaging change needs deploy + console rollouts. For quick win, we can gate CI to only build sm_86 and sm_80 SASS, others PTX.
Tyler K: Also audit our use of `--compress-all` vs `--compress-all` + `strip`. Sometimes `cuobjdump` shows duplicated symbols after LTO. We should `cuobjdump --list` artifacts to inspect.
Dana L: Actionable: Chris to try a branch with: `-gencode=arch=compute_86,code=sm_86 -gencode=arch=compute_80,code=sm_80 -gencode=arch=compute_70,code=compute_70` + disable `-flto` for the build job. Run artifact size + cuobjdump diff.
Chris W: Will do. Also adding a small python script to parse NVCC map output to compute per-sm contribution.
Olivia M: Long-term, we should update the toolchain RFC: decide default gencode whitelist per artifact (hosted vs dedicated) and an opt-in per model for SASS vs PTX. This will prevent surprise size regressions.
Sophie R: Also add a CI size gate that inspects `nvdisasm`/`cuobjdump` to detect duplicate PTX blocks — fails early.
Tyler K: FYI, I've seen `--generate-line-info` cause big jump in section tables; consider stripping lineinfo in release artifacts.
InfraBot: Ticket created: #INF-3142 "ci: nvcc gencode whitelist + size gate for attention kernels" assigned to Chris W
Chris W: Thanks. I'll post the branch + preliminary numbers in this thread once ready. :thumbsup:
Olivia M: Thanks — if you want I can help craft the fallback PTX-only run for older hardware matrix.
Chris W: Appreciate it. Will ping when the branch is up.
